title: Private Deployments: VPC & On‑Prem Reference, Day‑2 Ops, Upgrade/Rollback, and Customer Requirements
author: Elena Rodriguez
body:
Summary

This page consolidates our reference guidance for private deployments of Redwood Inference: VPC-hosted customer deployments and on-prem (air-gapped) packaging. It covers supported reference architectures, pre-requisites, the on-prem packaging and installer model, detailed day-2 operational runbooks (monitoring, backup, scaling, incident response), and step-by-step upgrade and rollback procedures. The document also includes a customer requirements checklist (network, security, capacity) used by Solutions Engineering and Sales.

Goals

- Provide a single, maintained reference for deployment engineers and customer SREs.
- Reduce time-to-first-success for private deployments by standardizing checks and runbooks.
- Minimize risk during upgrades and Day-2 operations through tested procedures and verification steps.

Supported deployment modes

1) VPC-managed private deployment
- Customer provisions a VPC/subnet(s) per our network template.
- Redwood control-plane endpoints are reachable over mutually authenticated TLS and optional PrivateLink/Peering.
- Data plane (inference) runs in customer VPC or in a dedicated account per contract.

2) On-prem (air-gapped) deployment
- Packaging includes an offline installer bundle and an ops bundle (images, manifests, upgrade tooling).
- Customer provides an immutable host cluster (Kubernetes >=1.26 or OpenShift 4.12) or bare-metal nodes managed by our on-prem runtime shim.

Reference architectures (high level)

Table: Reference sizing and topology guidance

- Small (Proof-of-Concept)
  - 1 control-plane node (customer-managed or Redwood-hosted), 3 inference worker GPUs (e.g., 3x A10G/RTX6000)
  - Use-case: low-throughput testing, <50 concurrent requests, bursty latency tolerant

- Medium (Production)
  - 3 control-plane replicas (HA), 6-12 GPU workers (A100 40GB or equivalent), dedicated Redis caching service, internal ingress
  - Use-case: steady production traffic, 200-1,000 qps aggregate depending on model size and batching

- Large (Enterprise)
  - Multi-AZ control-plane, 20+ GPU workers (mixture of A100 and T4 for mixed workloads), autoscaling pools, dedicated NFS/CSI storage for artifacts
  - Use-case: multi-tenant within org, SLA 99.9% + strict latency SLOs

Networking and security pre-requisites

- IP ranges and firewall rules: allow control-plane CIDR, health-check probes, and outbound to Redwood update endpoints (for non-air-gapped mode).
- TLS: mTLS for control-plane <-> agent comms; customer Furnished TLS certs (ACME or enterprise CA) supported.
- IAM/Service Accounts: Kubernetes ServiceAccount for runtime components; cloud roles for S3/EBS access where applicable.
- KMS/HSM: integration points for key management; if required, document customer KMS endpoints and key rotation policy.

On-prem packaging and installer model

- Bundle contents:
  - OCI image tarball (runtime images)
  - Helm charts and kustomize overlays for target k8s versions
  - Offline license and activation token
  - Installation CLI (linux binary) with interactive and non-interactive modes
  - Upgrade tool with dry-run verification

- Installer modes:
  1) Interactive: step-by-step prompts for air-gapped customers; validates node labels, kernel params, and container runtime versions.
  2) CI/CD friendly: non-interactive mode with a inputs YAML file (example below).

Example install inputs YAML (example snippet)

api_version: v1
cluster_name: redwood-customer-poc
control_plane_replicas: 3
worker_gpu_type: a100-40gb
storage_class: fast-ssd
network_policy: calico
license_token: REPLACE_WITH_TOKEN

Day-2 operations (runbooks)

A. Observability & Monitoring
- Required telemetry: node GPU utilization (nvidia-smi exporter), per-model QPS, per-route latency P50/P95/P99, KV cache hit rate, request queue depth.
- Dashboards: Redwood Console integration provides token-level cost and latency breakdown. Pre-built Grafana dashboards are included in the bundle.
- Alerts (recommended thresholds):
  - GPU memory utilization > 85% for 5m -> alert owners and consider autoscaling or model downscaling
  - P99 latency > 2x baseline SLO for 10m -> page oncall and capture sample requests
  - KV cache hit rate < 50% and cache miss growth -> investigate traffic pattern changes

B. Backups & Artifact retention
- Backups: periodic snapshot of model artifacts (S3 or NFS) and Redis persistence for KV cache where applicable.
- Frequency: daily snapshot of critical artifacts; weekly full snapshot for larger customers.
- Retention: default 30 days for snapshots; configurable per contract.

C. Routine maintenance
- Node replacement: drain node (kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data), remove GPU-specific local caches, re-labelling and rejoin cluster.
- Model rollout: use canary percentage rollout via our control-plane API; observe telemetry for degradation during 15-60 minute canary.

D. Scaling
- Horizontal scaling: add worker nodes to GPU pool; ensure autoscaler monitors GPU utilization and queue depth.
- Vertical scaling: replace instance types for greater GPU memory; requires draining workers and model warm-up after restart.

E. Incident handling (short procedure)
1) Detect: threshold alert triggers and automated tracing links point to impacted model/service.
2) Triage: capture recent requests, fertility of reruns, and endpoint mapping.
3) Mitigate: automatic fallback to smaller model variant or to hosted Redwood API (if contract allows).
4) Fix: deploy patch or rollback (see upgrade/rollback section).
5) Postmortem: run standard incident-review template and update runbooks.

Upgrade and rollback procedures

Principles:
- Always run upgrades in a canary-first fashion.
- Maintain a tested rollback artifact and verification checklist before changing production traffic.
- Keep changes small and timed during agreed maintenance windows for larger upgrades.

Pre-upgrade checklist:
1) Validate current cluster health: all pods Running, no pending PVCs, control-plane SLOs met for 48h.
2) Backup model artifacts and DBs; snapshot PVs and Redis.
3) Ensure upgrade bundle signature verified and hashes match.
4) Confirm rollback artifact exists and is accessible.

Canary upgrade steps (numbered):
1) Deploy control-plane minor patch to 1 replica in canary namespace.
2) Run smoke tests: health endpoints, example inference requests, and auth flows (automated).
3) If smoke tests pass, expand to 10% of control-plane replicas for 30 minutes while monitoring key metrics (latency, errors, token/unit costs).
4) If no regressions, progressively increase to 50% for 1 hour then to 100% during maintenance window.

Rollback steps (emergency):
1) Immediately switch routed traffic to previously verified model variant or hosted Redwood fallback.
2) Use upgrade tool to revert control-plane images to prior SHA (installer supports rollback --target-sha).
3) Redeploy control-plane replicas with previous manifests and restart workers with previous image set.
4) Verify operational health: end-to-end smoke tests, dashboard metrics, and internal sampled requests.

Verification checklist after rollback:
- Endpoints return expected responses for a representative sample of prompts.
- Latency and error rates are back within baseline.
- No data loss detected in snapshots or logs.

Customer requirements library (checklist for pre-sales and SEs)

Network & Security
- Provided VPC/subnet CIDRs: yes/no
- BGP/DirectConnect or equivalent for cross-region connectivity: yes/no
- Firewall rules to allow control-plane CIDR: yes/no
- TLS: enterprise CA certs available: yes/no
- KMS/HSM details if required: yes/no

Capacity & Hardware
- Expected qps and concurrency
- Preferred GPU types and count
- Storage: PV capacity and IOPS requirements
- Available bandwidth between control-plane and worker nodes

Operational expectations
- Maintenance window constraints (days/times)
- RTO/RPO contractual targets
- Backup retention & snapshot window
- Support escalation path and contact info

Deliverables from Redwood for handoff
- Installer bundle and operator binary
- Helm charts/kustomize overlays
- Pre-built Grafana dashboards and alert rules
- Runbooks and SRE playbook for the customer
- Upgrade/rollback artifacts and verification scripts

Appendix: Useful commands and scripts

- Drain a worker node:
  kubectl drain <node-name> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data

- Manual model inference smoke test (curl):
  curl -X POST https://<inference-endpoint>/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"prompt":"hello","max_tokens":16}'

- Snapshot PV to S3 (example wrapper):
  ./tools/pv-snapshot --pv-name model-artifacts --target-s3 s3://customer-snapshots/redwood --compress

- Verify upgrade bundle signature:
  openssl dgst -sha256 -verify public.pem -signature bundle.sig bundle.tar.gz
